Uber safety

By: Ntokozo Miya | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
After testimonies about horrific attacks inside Uber taxis surfaced in court recently, we ask: can the online taxi hailing service really guarantee its passengers and drivers a safe trip?

Unique Selling Point:
Uber is a popular taxi service that many people rely on precisely because it is believed to be safe and reliable. It is in the public's interest to be aware of any service that might not be as safe as it is perceived or marketed to be.

Summary:
Four men are on trial at the Gauteng High Court, facing charges of rape, robbery, assault and kidnapping. The men, one of whom was an Uber driver, allegedly targeted passengers who requested the service. Their MO is believed to have been to operate in three's with one man driving the car while two more hid in the boot, waiting to pounce on unsuspecting passengers. The men are accused of sexually assaulting seven women, demanding their ATM pin numbers and driving around with the victims to various ATMs to make withdrawals from their bank accounts.
Attorney Ulrich Roux is representing 2 of the victims in the criminal case and next month, Roux together with other attorneys for the victims will initiate civil action against Uber.
Unfortunately, Uber is no stranger to sex abuse allegations against their drivers across the globe. As such, it is reasonable to expect that the taxi service would be on top of their game as far as passenger safety is concerned – so, how did Uber safety measures fail these local women?
Also, we follow up on the SAPS investigation into a chemical attack which left Uber driver Kgomotso Tiro scarred for life. A passenger poured a chemical believed to be acid on Kgomotso's hands and face, and then set him alight. Kgomotso spent 2 weeks at the Helen Joseph Hospital in Johannesburg. An investigation into the attack was launched but Kgomotso say the police are bungling the case and not pursuing leads as they should be. - what hindered the investigation into Kgomotso's attack?

Further information:
-In 2018, Uber global was reportedly valued at $72 billion and facilitated over 15 million rides daily. The service has over 1 million users in SA.
-The service is no stranger to sexual assault scandals. Most of the sex abuse cases come from complaints made by female passengers who are often raped during the robbery.
-A 2018 CNN investigation revealed that 103 Uber drivers in US were charged with sexual assault in the previous four years. At least 31 drivers have been convicted for crimes ranging from forcible touching and false imprisonment to rape, and dozens of criminal and civil cases are pending.
-Civil lawsuits against Uber are so common in the US that law firm Estey and Bomberger specialize in litigations and advertise on their appropriately named website – www.ubersexualassaultlawyer.com.
-In 2016, almost half of all drivers working for a private hire or taxi operator that were convicted of a sexual offence in London last year were driving for Uber, data from the London Metropolitan Police revealed. A total of 164 drivers were reported for such attacks in 2016.
-The problem is so rife that in 2017, Uber's license to operate in London was suspended, with health and safety reasons being cited.
-Uber SA said they have introduced a number of safety features such as Real Time ID Check, Trusted Contacts, In-App Emergency Button and 24/7 phone support.
-Taxi attacks are not exclusive to Uber. Just last week in SA, two women reported that a Taxify driver stabbed them when they failed to pay for the trip. The women dispute that they didn't pay for the trip and say the motive was robbery because the driver took the money they had.
-In February 2018, a Taxify driver allegedly showed a passenger his private parts during the trip.

Press Release:


e-Hailing Cab Service Safety
If you’ve ever been left stranded without transport after a late night out or you’ve had to rush to the airport in the early hours of the morning, then you’ll understand why e-hailing cab services have become so popular. They’re fast, convenient and right at your finger-tips. But what happens when a driver turns on the passenger? Kidnapping, assault and rape – these are some of the horror stories from users of the e-hailing cab service which have emerged at the Gauteng High Court. Carte Blanche asks: just how safe are its users?
Producer: Ntokozo Miya
Presenter: Devi Sankaree Govender
Watch the trailer


Script:


UBER ATTACKS – FINAL MIX SCRIPT

FOCUS – To what extent can Uber guarantee the safety of its passengers and drivers?
VO - Tracy Stockhall is one of about 1 million people who signed up to Uber after it launched in South Africa in 2013.

The Uber taxi hailing app requires users to register with their personal details and bank account information. To order a cab, users enter their location and destination in the app, which then calculates the cost of the trip and confirms the booking.

Regular customers consider Uber a safe alternative but for Tracy, it turned into a nightmare.
Tracy Stockhall – Uber passenger

00:03:09:22 – I got into the car and I sat in the front seat.
00:03:54:03 – Suddenly someone put a wire around my neck, it came from the back of the car.
VO – Tracy thought it was just her and the driver in the cab she ordered after a night out but she was wrong. There were two other passengers, both men, and they immediately tried to subdue her.
Tracy Stockhall – Uber passenger

00:04:09:05 – ... They must have come from the boot into the back of the car.
00:19:28:24 – The guys are quite tall so how they got in the boot, how they climbed through without me knowing – I was quite surprised. I never would have thought there were other guys in that car.
00:04:09:05 – ... they jumped out from the back seat right behind me, put a wire around my neck and started to strangle me.
00:04:30:13 – ... I managed to pull the wire away from me, and I hit the driver, punched him.
00:05:09:24 – ... All I wanted to do was get out of that car.
00:06:26:12 – I just jumped out without my bag and my phone and everything.
00:05:38:22 – I hit the tar and I scraped off skin on my face and my whole body. I bumped my head.
VO – Fortunately, Tracy’s attackers didn't chase after her when she jumped out of the moving car.
Devi – 00:23:30:10 – And you had to pay for that trip?

Tracy – Well, they reversed the charges but initially, yes. 00:07:37:14 – We got the bill the next day. It came through on email with the amount and all of the supposed driver’s registration, all his details so he was a registered Uber driver.
VO – Grandmother Susan Dey was not so lucky. Also a longtime Uber customer, her ride would change her life forever.

She was overpowered and strangled by the driver and two men who also emerged from the boot of her Uber.
Susan Dey – Uber passenger

00:51:09:19 – I tried to open the door but couldn’t see where the door handle was and I actually pulled the window down. I put my arm out and I was waving it and shouting and they pulled it even tighter again and threatened to kill me again.
VO – The men shoved Susan in the boot.
Susan Dey – Uber passenger

00:58:45:16 – ...and he hit me in the kidneys and he grabbed my one breast and pulled it.
VO – They drove to a secluded area and then, the driver gave her instructions.
Susan Dey – Uber passenger


01:01:28:24 – He said to put my head back into the boot and bring your legs and the bottom half of your torso out. I was lying with my upper body and head in the boot and my lower body and out onto the backseat on top of the back rest...
01:02:08:10 – ... and then he raped me.
VO – Susan’s Uber ride from hell lasted for about six hours.
Susan Dey – Uber passenger

01:04:12:04 – Two guys took me, one took me by the arms and the other one took me by the legs and then they swung me over the barrier.

01:04:27:08 – Devi – Like a sack?

Susan – Like a sack, and threw me down a steep embankment.
VO – A good Samaritan helped Susan get to safety and call her son.
Susan Dey – Uber passenger

01:11:48:02 - ... I just looked up at him and I said: Mike I didn’t tell you on the phone (cries) but I have to tell you now that I was raped. You can imagine – no son, no daughter should ever need to know that about their 63-year-old mother, really, you know.
VO – Uber also initially billed for the Susan for the trip, confirming that this must have been a legitimate trip with one of their drivers.
Susan Dey – Uber passenger

01:18:13:19 – ... Uber tried to say it wasn’t an Uber driver but it turned out, finally, that it absolutely was an Uber driver. ... The denial was immediate and I said: tell me how is it possible that you bill me for the ride from Montecasino up until when they stop the vehicle and threw me in the boot?
LINK - 02:57:09:02 – Tracy and Susan just wanted to get home safely but instead, when they booked Ubers back in 2016, they got rides to hell.
VO – Tracy and Susan are victims of the men dubbed the Uber gang, consisting of an Uber driver and his accomplices. The Uber gang kidnapped, robbed and raped passengers who hailed cabs using the app. (PLEASE CREDIT TIMESLIVE FOR UBER GANG PIC)

Susan’s daughter, musician Tamara Dey, was devastated when she heard what happened to her mother.
Tamara Dey – Susan’s daughter

00:32:01:00 – I don’t think I’ll ever be the same after getting that phone call. Having something like that happen to you is every woman’s worst nightmare but you kind of don’t imagine that it’s going to happen to your mother.
VO – Uber isn’t the only e-hailing service with safety complaints, but it has been under the spotlight.

According to a CNN report in January, Uber handles 1200 complaints in North America each week, many of them sexual.

And in London in June last year, Uber was granted a 15-month probationary operating license after it was suspended for safety reasons.
Tamara Dey – Susan’s daughter

00:37:44:15 – ... Only after my mom’s attack I obviously started to pick up on any news about Uber around the world. I was horrified at people taking advantage of their system or being able to take advantage of their system in ways like this around the world. None of us knew about this.
VO – The Uber gang members were arrested in 2016 and denied bail. The men are currently on trial at the Gauteng High Court.
LINK - 03:06:06:16 – But concerns around the safety of Uber are not limited to four cases back in 2016, we’ve received reports of more recent attacks.
VO – This man asked that we hide his identity to protect his son, who, in September last year, caught an Uber home from his matric dance. En route, the teenager phoned his parents, sounding incoherent.
‘Timothy’ - Parent (please distort voice and add blur)

03:07:55:03 – I then asked him to send me a location and he sent a location and I discovered he was in the city centre.
03:08:21:12 – ... They robbed him. His wallet was gone.
03:08:37:13 – ... He had marks on his neck.
VO – The family reported the robbery and assault on their son by the driver to Uber.
‘Timothy’ - Parent (please distort voice and add blur)

03:10:20:21 – When I asked them what they were going to do about it, it was a matter of they could do nothing about it because our South African police must do something about it.
VO – The family did not pursue the complaint to avoid traumatising the youngster, who was studying for his matric finals at the time.

Tracy and Susan have instructed their attorney, Ulrich Roux, to institute a lawsuit against Uber.
Ulrich Roux – Attorney

01:53:05:15 – ... They were placed under the erroneous belief, by Uber, that they would be safe, that they would be secure and that was obviously not the case.
VO – Roux says Uber can't advertise safe rides and then not provide them.
Ulrich Roux – Attorney

02:11:05:23 – ... if you make that claim, that you are safe and reliable and secure, then you must make sure that you have proper systems in place to ensure that safety.
VO – In the intimate confines of vehicles, it’s not just passengers who are at risk. The drivers are also at the mercy of whoever enters their car.

There have been numerous reports of Uber drivers attacked by competing cab drivers as well as passengers.

In 2017, Kgomotso Tiro’s life changed when he picked up a drunken passenger.
Kgomotso Tiro – Uber driver

02:20:43:20 – ...He just poured me with acid on my side, on my face. ... I tried to push him and try to fight for the bottle. That’s how it ended up on my hands, as you see my hands like this.
02:21:15:00 – ... He set me alight on the jacket. I was on flames. And then he took my car. He drove away.
02:23:23:12 – I was in hospital for 2 weeks and I was discharged. I stayed at home for almost 6 to 8 months with no income.
VO – A year and a half later, Kgomotso’s case remains unsolved. SAPS Captain Kay Makhubela says the investigation is ongoing.
Kay Makhubela – SAPS

02:57:39:02 – There was a similar case in Florida where we were trying to link the suspect with the same case.
02:58:39:20 – ... We are following all the leads which are coming forward to us to make sure that the matter is finalised.
VO – Following the Carte Blanche interview, Kgomotso’s case has been assigned to a senior official.

Kgomotso is back at Uber, and is more vigilant when on duty.
Kgomotso Tiro – Uber driver

02:22:55:08 – ... I’m driving and I’m more careful now because I have to choose the trip I take. I have to choose the area that I work at. I don’t just pick up any trips. Sometimes if I arrive at your place after requesting and I feel like this is dodgy, I’m not going to pick you up. I just cancel the trip and go.
02:22:26:16 – It is very dangerous nowadays, especially with cash trips. With cards, you feel much safer even though you are not that safe but you’re still safe because with card, they can be traced.
LINK - 03:05:09:14 – With both passengers and drivers feeling insecure, to what extent can the online taxi hailing service guarantee its passengers and drivers a safe trip?
VO – Carte Blanche requested an on-camera interview with Uber, but the company cited the ongoing court case as a reason not to talk to us.
LINK - 02:56:24:23 – Eventually, Uber responded in writing but it’s impossible to interrogate their views in the absence of a conversation.
VO - Uber says the attacks were “deeply upsetting”, and that it had subsequently "developed a number of safety features".

With the introduction of cash payments, Uber drivers are easy targets for robbers and as such, drivers can now decide beforehand if they want to accept cash trips.
VO - To protect passengers, Uber says it drivers undergo criminal and fingerprint verification checks.
Riders can also make use of the app’s emergency button and 24/7 phone support.
According to Uber, the only way to access rider details is if one is logged into the app as the driver.
More information on Uber’s safety features is available on the company’s website.
This driver, who wanted to remain anonymous, also says some drivers shared their profiles with people not registered with Uber.
‘Thabo’ - Uber driver (please distort voice and add blur)

02:36:51:10 – ... He just goes online and maybe gives it to his friend to keep working.
02:37:24:01 – ... People are trying to make a lot of money. Sometimes you get tired, you need to go rest. If you still have hours, someone else might come in to work.
VO – Criminals can also steal a driver’s phone and use the app to prey on passengers.
‘Thabo’ - Uber driver (please distort voice and add blur)

02:38:06:11 – Maybe they were hijacked or something, and the phone was robbed, then someone comes in and uses their profile before they report it – then it is a problem.
VO – Tracy says she still has nightmares about what could have happened if she hadn’t escaped.
Tracy Stockhall – Uber passenger

00:08:03:00 – I would have been raped, tied up in the boot, driven around and dumped in the middle of nowhere, exactly what happened to the other victims.
VO – Susan says her horrific Uber trip left her so traumatised, she struggled to be productive at work.
Susan Dey – Uber passenger

01:15:12:23 – ... I did what I could to work. I thought I was okay but obviously I wasn’t. I was incompetent, to be frank. At the end of my contract, which was 5, 6 months later, they didn’t renew it.
01:15:40:09 – So there I was, 63, actually just 64 by then, with no job, a bond which I couldn’t pay so I lost the house. I basically lost my life that I had worked really hard to achieve.
VO – And this family is steering clear of Uber.
‘Timothy’ - Parent (please distort voice and add blur)

03:11:31:13 – Prior to the incident, he used Uber fairly often. After the incident, none of my kids will ever drive in an Uber again.

Susan Dey – Uber passenger 00:51:09:19 – I tried to open the door but couldn’t see where the door handle was and I actually pulled the window down. I put my arm out and I was waving it and shouting and they pulled it even tighter again and threatened to kill me again. VO – The men shoved Susan in the boot. Susan Dey – Uber passenger 00:58:45:16 – ...and he hit me in the kidneys and he grabbed my one breast and pulled it. VO – They drove to a secluded area and then, the driver gave her instructions. Susan Dey – Uber passenger 01:01:28:24 – He said to put my head back into the boot and bring your legs and the bottom half of your torso out. I was lying with my upper body and head in the boot and my lower body and out onto the backseat on top of the back rest... 01:02:08:10 – ... and then he raped me. VO – Susan’s Uber ride from hell lasted for about six hours. Susan Dey – Uber passenger 01:04:12:04 – Two guys took me, one took me by the arms and the other one took me by the legs and then they swung me over the barrier. 01:04:27:08 – Devi – Like a sack? Susan – Like a sack, and threw me down a steep embankment. VO – A good Samaritan helped Susan get to safety and call her son. Susan Dey – Uber passenger 01:11:48:02 - ... I just looked up at him and I said: Mike I didn’t tell you on the phone (cries) but I have to tell you now that I was raped. You can imagine – no son, no daughter should ever need to know that about their 63-year-old mother, really, you know. VO – Uber also initially billed for the Susan for the trip, confirming that this must have been a legitimate trip with one of their drivers. Susan Dey – Uber passenger 01:18:13:19 – ... Uber tried to say it wasn’t an Uber driver but it turned out, finally, that it absolutely was an Uber driver. ... The denial was immediate and I said: tell me how is it possible that you bill me for the ride from Montecasino up until when they stop the vehicle and threw me in the boot? LINK - 02:57:09:02 – Tracy and Susan just wanted to get home safely but instead, when they booked Ubers back in 2016, they got rides to hell. VO – Tracy and Susan are victims of the men dubbed the Uber gang, consisting of an Uber driver and his accomplices. The Uber gang kidnapped, robbed and raped passengers who hailed cabs using the app. (PLEASE CREDIT TIMESLIVE FOR UBER GANG PIC) Susan’s daughter, musician Tamara Dey, was devastated when she heard what happened to her mother. Tamara Dey – Susan’s daughter 00:32:01:00 – I don’t think I’ll ever be the same after getting that phone call. Having something like that happen to you is every woman’s worst nightmare but you kind of don’t imagine that it’s going to happen to your mother. VO – Uber isn’t the only e-hailing service with safety complaints, but it has been under the spotlight. According to a CNN report in January, Uber handles 1200 complaints in North America each week, many of them sexual. And in London in June last year, Uber was granted a 15-month probationary operating license after it was suspended for safety reasons. Tamara Dey – Susan’s daughter 00:37:44:15 – ... Only after my mom’s attack I obviously started to pick up on any news about Uber around the world. I was horrified at people taking advantage of their system or being able to take advantage of their system in ways like this around the world. None of us knew about this. VO – The Uber gang members were arrested in 2016 and denied bail. The men are currently on trial at the Gauteng High Court. LINK - 03:06:06:16 – But concerns around the safety of Uber are not limited to four cases back in 2016, we’ve received reports of more recent attacks. VO – This man asked that we hide his identity to protect his son, who, in September last year, caught an Uber home from his matric dance. En route, the teenager phoned his parents, sounding incoherent. ‘Timothy’ - Parent (please distort voice and add blur) 03:07:55:03 – I then asked him to send me a location and he sent a location and I discovered he was in the city centre. 03:08:21:12 – ... They robbed him. His wallet was gone. 03:08:37:13 – ... He had marks on his neck. VO – The family reported the robbery and assault on their son by the driver to Uber. ‘Timothy’ - Parent (please distort voice and add blur) 03:10:20:21 – When I asked them what they were going to do about it, it was a matter of they could do nothing about it because our South African police must do something about it. VO – The family did not pursue the complaint to avoid traumatising the youngster, who was studying for his matric finals at the time. Tracy and Susan have instructed their attorney, Ulrich Roux, to institute a lawsuit against Uber. Ulrich Roux – Attorney 01:53:05:15 – ... They were placed under the erroneous belief, by Uber, that they would be safe, that they would be secure and that was obviously not the case. VO – Roux says Uber can't advertise safe rides and then not provide them. Ulrich Roux – Attorney 02:11:05:23 – ... if you make that claim, that you are safe and reliable and secure, then you must make sure that you have proper systems in place to ensure that safety. VO – In the intimate confines of vehicles, it’s not just passengers who are at risk. The drivers are also at the mercy of whoever enters their car. There have been numerous reports of Uber drivers attacked by competing cab drivers as well as passengers. In 2017, Kgomotso Tiro’s life changed when he picked up a drunken passenger. Kgomotso Tiro – Uber driver 02:20:43:20 – ...He just poured me with acid on my side, on my face. ... I tried to push him and try to fight for the bottle. That’s how it ended up on my hands, as you see my hands like this. 02:21:15:00 – ... He set me alight on the jacket. I was on flames. And then he took my car. He drove away. 02:23:23:12 – I was in hospital for 2 weeks and I was discharged. I stayed at home for almost 6 to 8 months with no income. VO – A year and a half later, Kgomotso’s case remains unsolved. SAPS Captain Kay Makhubela says the investigation is ongoing. Kay Makhubela – SAPS 02:57:39:02 – There was a similar case in Florida where we were trying to link the suspect with the same case. 02:58:39:20 – ... We are following all the leads which are coming forward to us to make sure that the matter is finalised. VO – Following the Carte Blanche interview, Kgomotso’s case has been assigned to a senior official. Kgomotso is back at Uber, and is more vigilant when on duty. Kgomotso Tiro – Uber driver 02:22:55:08 – ... I’m driving and I’m more careful now because I have to choose the trip I take. I have to choose the area that I work at. I don’t just pick up any trips. Sometimes if I arrive at your place after requesting and I feel like this is dodgy, I’m not going to pick you up. I just cancel the trip and go. 02:22:26:16 – It is very dangerous nowadays, especially with cash trips. With cards, you feel much safer even though you are not that safe but you’re still safe because with card, they can be traced. LINK - 03:05:09:14 – With both passengers and drivers feeling insecure, to what extent can the online taxi hailing service guarantee its passengers and drivers a safe trip? VO – Carte Blanche requested an on-camera interview with Uber, but the company cited the ongoing court case as a reason not to talk to us. LINK - 02:56:24:23 – Eventually, Uber responded in writing but it’s impossible to interrogate their views in the absence of a conversation. VO - Uber says the attacks were “deeply upsetting”, and that it had subsequently "developed a number of safety features". With the introduction of cash payments, Uber drivers are easy targets for robbers and as such, drivers can now decide beforehand if they want to accept cash trips. VO - To protect passengers, Uber says it drivers undergo criminal and fingerprint verification checks. Riders can also make use of the app’s emergency button and 24/7 phone support. According to Uber, the only way to access rider details is if one is logged into the app as the driver. More information on Uber’s safety features is available on the company’s website. This driver, who wanted to remain anonymous, also says some drivers shared their profiles with people not registered with Uber. ‘Thabo’ - Uber driver (please distort voice and add blur) 02:36:51:10 – ... He just goes online and maybe gives it to his friend to keep working. 02:37:24:01 – ... People are trying to make a lot of money. Sometimes you get tired, you need to go rest. If you still have hours, someone else might come in to work. VO – Criminals can also steal a driver’s phone and use the app to prey on passengers. ‘Thabo’ - Uber driver (please distort voice and add blur) 02:38:06:11 – Maybe they were hijacked or something, and the phone was robbed, then someone comes in and uses their profile before they report it – then it is a problem. VO – Tracy says she still has nightmares about what could have happened if she hadn’t escaped. Tracy Stockhall – Uber passenger 00:08:03:00 – I would have been raped, tied up in the boot, driven around and dumped in the middle of nowhere, exactly what happened to the other victims. VO – Susan says her horrific Uber trip left her so traumatised, she struggled to be productive at work. Susan Dey – Uber passenger 01:15:12:23 – ... I did what I could to work. I thought I was okay but obviously I wasn’t. I was incompetent, to be frank. At the end of my contract, which was 5, 6 months later, they didn’t renew it. 01:15:40:09 – So there I was, 63, actually just 64 by then, with no job, a bond which I couldn’t pay so I lost the house. I basically lost my life that I had worked really hard to achieve. VO – And this family is steering clear of Uber. ‘Timothy’ - Parent (please distort voice and add blur) 03:11:31:13 – Prior to the incident, he used Uber fairly often. After the incident, none of my kids will ever drive in an Uber again.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): After testimonies about horrific attacks inside Uber taxis surfaced in court recently, we ask: can the online taxi hailing service really guarantee its passengers and drivers a safe trip?
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Uber is a popular taxi service that many people rely on precisely because it is believed to be safe and reliable. It is in the public's interest to be aware of any service that might not be as safe as it is perceived or marketed to be.
metadata.Summary: Four men are on trial at the Gauteng High Court, facing charges of rape, robbery, assault and kidnapping. The men, one of whom was an Uber driver, allegedly targeted passengers who requested the service. Their MO is believed to have been to operate in three's with one man driving the car while two more hid in the boot, waiting to pounce on unsuspecting passengers. The men are accused of sexually assaulting seven women, demanding their ATM pin numbers and driving around with the victims to various ATMs to make withdrawals from their bank accounts. Attorney Ulrich Roux is representing 2 of the victims in the criminal case and next month, Roux together with other attorneys for the victims will initiate civil action against Uber. Unfortunately, Uber is no stranger to sex abuse allegations against their drivers across the globe. As such, it is reasonable to expect that the taxi service would be on top of their game as far as passenger safety is concerned – so, how did Uber safety measures fail these local women? Also, we follow up on the SAPS investigation into a chemical attack which left Uber driver Kgomotso Tiro scarred for life. A passenger poured a chemical believed to be acid on Kgomotso's hands and face, and then set him alight. Kgomotso spent 2 weeks at the Helen Joseph Hospital in Johannesburg. An investigation into the attack was launched but Kgomotso say the police are bungling the case and not pursuing leads as they should be. - what hindered the investigation into Kgomotso's attack?
metadata.Further information: -In 2018, Uber global was reportedly valued at $72 billion and facilitated over 15 million rides daily. The service has over 1 million users in SA. -The service is no stranger to sexual assault scandals. Most of the sex abuse cases come from complaints made by female passengers who are often raped during the robbery. -A 2018 CNN investigation revealed that 103 Uber drivers in US were charged with sexual assault in the previous four years. At least 31 drivers have been convicted for crimes ranging from forcible touching and false imprisonment to rape, and dozens of criminal and civil cases are pending. -Civil lawsuits against Uber are so common in the US that law firm Estey and Bomberger specialize in litigations and advertise on their appropriately named website – www.ubersexualassaultlawyer.com. -In 2016, almost half of all drivers working for a private hire or taxi operator that were convicted of a sexual offence in London last year were driving for Uber, data from the London Metropolitan Police revealed. A total of 164 drivers were reported for such attacks in 2016. -The problem is so rife that in 2017, Uber's license to operate in London was suspended, with health and safety reasons being cited. -Uber SA said they have introduced a number of safety features such as Real Time ID Check, Trusted Contacts, In-App Emergency Button and 24/7 phone support. -Taxi attacks are not exclusive to Uber. Just last week in SA, two women reported that a Taxify driver stabbed them when they failed to pay for the trip. The women dispute that they didn't pay for the trip and say the motive was robbery because the driver took the money they had. -In February 2018, a Taxify driver allegedly showed a passenger his private parts during the trip.
